title: 6. 10-Year Financial Forensics, Cash Conversion & Balance Sheet
summary_box: Across FY15–FY26, India Glycols grew sales from ₹2,579 Cr to ₹4,211 Cr. Net profit swung from a -₹89 Cr loss to ₹293 Cr. Yet 3-year ROE averaged a modest 10.4% (11.3% latest), while Free Cash Flow stayed negative across FY22–FY26 due to distillery capex. After the September 2026 demerger, Total Assets reset from ₹6,523 Cr to ₹2,611 Cr and Borrowings halved from ₹1,691 Cr to ₹826 Cr. The cleaner balance sheet now awaits proof of higher standalone ROE.

epigraph.quote: Income statements are opinions; balance sheets and ten-year cash flow tables are the unvarnished biography of every capital allocation decision.
epigraph.author: Forensic Accounting Maxim

web_blocks.html: Reading India Glycols' 10-year financial record requires separating two distinct eras [1]. First comes the FY15–FY26 combined conglomerate era, followed by the September 2026 post-demerger balance-sheet reset. From FY15 to FY26, consolidated revenue rose from ₹2,579 Cr to ₹4,211 Cr [1]. Operating Profit expanded more than fivefold from ₹124 Cr (4.8% OPM) to ₹649 Cr (15.4% OPM). Over the same span, Net Profit recovered from -₹89 Cr in FY15 and -₹57 Cr in FY16 to ₹293 Cr in FY26 [1].

web_blocks.caption: 10-Year Consolidated Profit & Loss Statement (FY2015–FY2026 & TTM, ₹ Cr)
web_blocks.takeaway: Operating margins expanded structurally from 4.8% (FY15) to 15% (FY26), while TTM reflects the partial-year transition to post-demerger continuing operations in H1 FY27 [1].

web_blocks.html: Forensic Diagnosis of the Bear Case (Low 3-Year ROE & High Borrowing Cost): Despite rising profits, two structural weaknesses stand out in the historical record [1]. First, 3-year average ROE remained a modest 10.4%, with 11.3% latest ROE and 12.4% ROCE [1]. Equity reserves swelled from ₹1,138 Cr in FY21 to ₹2,899 Cr in FY26 via the ₹239.88 Cr Clariant exceptional gain (FY22) and the ₹466.99 Cr preferential issue (Nov 2025) [1][11][15]. Meanwhile, heavy capex lifted Fixed Assets from ₹2,193 Cr in FY21 to ₹4,554 Cr in FY26, depressing asset turns until new distilleries ramped up. Second, borrowing costs were historically elevated, as interest expense climbed from ₹70 Cr in FY22 to ₹167 Cr in FY26. That implied a ~9.3%–10% cost on average borrowings [1][7]. As a result, CARE Ratings maintained CARE A- / CARE A2+ on Rating Watch with Developing Implications (RWD) in March 2026, noting 'average' debt coverage.

web_blocks.caption: 10-Year Consolidated Balance Sheet (Mar 2015–Sep 2026 Post-Demerger, ₹ Cr)
web_blocks.takeaway: The September 2026 column captures the demerger boundary: Total Assets shrank 60% (₹6,523 Cr → ₹2,611 Cr) and Borrowings fell 51% (₹1,691 Cr → ₹826 Cr) as Spirits and Ennature exited [1][2].

web_blocks.html: The September 2026 Balance-Sheet Reset: Comparing March 2026 (pre-demerger) to September 2026 (post-demerger) reveals a dramatically de-risked capital structure [1]. Total Assets dropped from ₹6,523 Cr to ₹2,611 Cr, while Fixed Assets fell from ₹4,554 Cr to ₹1,257 Cr. Borrowings were cut by more than half, falling from ₹1,691 Cr to ₹826 Cr [1]. That implies Debt-to-Equity of roughly 0.66x against ₹1,258 Cr of Equity Capital and Reserves. Meanwhile, Investments actually rose from ₹389 Cr to ₹422 Cr, reflecting the retained 49% stake in Clariant IGL Specialty Chemicals [1][10][16]. Shareholding disclosures also confirm 59.63% promoter ownership with Nil share pledge.

web_blocks.caption: 10-Year Consolidated Cash Flow & Free Cash Flow Conversion (FY2015–FY2026, ₹ Cr)
web_blocks.takeaway: CFO/EBITDA was strong in FY23 (123%), FY24 (108%), and FY26 (122%), yet cumulative FCF across FY22–FY26 was -₹914 Cr due to ₹2,400+ Cr of investing outflows [1].

web_blocks.caption: 10-Year Working Capital & Capital Efficiency Ratios (FY2015–FY2026)
web_blocks.takeaway: Debtor Days halved from 59 (FY23) to 30 (FY26) and Working Capital Days remained structurally negative (-49 days), cushioning cash conversion [1].

web_blocks.mechanism: Leading domestic manufacturer of phthalic anhydride whose selling prices track global petrochemical/crude-linked benchmarks while margins swing sharply with regional supply-demand spreads and multi-year brownfield capex cycles.
web_blocks.outcome_numbers: ROCE surged past 30% during tight spread peaks (FY21–FY22) before compressing back to single digits during global oversupply and capex digestion (FY24).
web_blocks.lesson_for_symbol: Indian mid-cap chemical producers that rely on spread cycles rarely compound linearly; true value depends on keeping net debt low enough (<1x equity) to survive trough spreads without equity dilution.

web_blocks.title: NARRATOR'S REFLECTION
paragraphs: Every number in the 10-year ledger points to the same fork in the road. Pre-demerger INDIAGLYCO was a high-capex, ~10% ROE, negative-FCF conglomerate whose debt peaked at ₹2,264 Cr in FY15 and ₹1,892 Cr in FY25.

Post-demerger INDIAGLYCO starts its standalone life in September 2026 with ₹826 Cr of debt, 0.66x Debt-to-Equity, and zero promoter pledges. It also holds ₹422 Cr of investments anchored by the Clariant JV alongside just ₹12 Cr/quarter in interest expense. If management avoids another debt-funded capex spree and lets cash accumulate, ROE and FCF can finally inflect upward. That earns a CYCLICAL_CONDITIONAL rating today with clear upgrade triggers ahead.

book_paragraphs: Open the ten-year ledger for India Glycols and you see two completely different stories depending on whether you stop at March 2026 or turn the page to September 2026. Over the full decade from FY15 to FY26, revenue climbed from ₹2,579 Cr to ₹4,211 Cr and operating margins marched from a distressed 4.8% to 15.4%. On the surface, it looked like a steady turnaround.

Yet the skeptics had real ammunition. Over the last three years, Return on Equity averaged just 10.4%—barely above the company's own ~9%–10% borrowing cost, which explains why CARE Ratings kept the credit rating at CARE A- with average debt-coverage remarks. Worse, from FY22 through FY26, free cash flow was negative every single year, totaling minus ₹914 Cr, because nearly every rupee of operating cash flow went straight back into building grain distilleries and ethanol plants.

Now turn the page to the September 2026 balance sheet. In one stroke, the demerger wiped 60% of the asset base off India Glycols' books—Total Assets dropped from ₹6,523 Cr to ₹2,611 Cr, Fixed Assets fell from ₹4,554 Cr to ₹1,257 Cr, and Borrowings were cut in half from ₹1,691 Cr to ₹826 Cr. Meanwhile, the ₹422 Cr Investments line—home to the 49% Clariant IGL joint venture—stayed right where it was.

That is the forensic heart of this audit. For ten years, you could rightly criticize India Glycols for low ROE, high interest bills, and negative free cash flow. Starting in FY27, the capital-hungry distilleries belong to IGL Spirits, the borrowings are down to 0.66 times equity, promoter pledges are zero, and quarterly interest is just ₹12 Cr. Whether this cleaner chemical shell can lift its standalone ROE above 14%–15% and convert profit into free cash flow will decide whether it remains a cyclical trade or graduates into a durable compounder.

book_callouts.title: NARRATOR'S REFLECTION
paragraphs: We have completed the price-blind forensic audit of India Glycols Limited without once glancing at its ticker price. With a CYCLICAL_CONDITIONAL quality verdict and PASS_WITH_WATCH KPI health, we are ready for Pass 2 to weigh valuation, expectations, and market structure.
